resolution_requirement.method: Cf from ITTC-1957 at the anchor Re -> u_tau/U = sqrt(Cf/2); y+ of the first cell centre = 0.5*u_tau_lb/nu_lb with nu_lb = u_lb*L/Re; delta/L = 0.37*Re^-0.2; cells = 26.66*L^3 (frozen domain padding 1/4/1/1/1/1 at 2.108L lateral extent)
resolution_requirement.conclusion: the anchor Re puts the first cell at y+ ~ 1.7e3-2.3e3 at the frozen ladder, i.e. the whole viscous layer is sub-grid; a wall-resolved lattice would need L ~ 2e5 cells per hull length (10^16 cells) and even a wall-model band (y+~500) needs L~450 / ~2e9 cells, 4.7x per dimension beyond the finest tier

measured.note: Re matching is exact by construction (nu_lb = u_lb*L/Re_anchor) and was verified from the reported lattice pair on the executed L=96 setup; the tiers are therefore admissible for a 3% judgement - there is simply no converged tier to judge

verdict.headline: The DTRC anchor Reynolds number is not reachable by the frozen D3Q19/MRT instrument at L=96/112/128: matching Re pins tau-0.5 at 1.2e-6..1.6e-6, which puts the first cell at y+ ~ 1.7e3-2.3e3, i.e. the whole viscous layer is sub-grid (delta ~ 1.4-1.8 cells). The frozen ladder could not be executed (measured 15-20 s/step at L=96 => 61-144 h per tier). The anchor-Re probes that WERE run never settle: at L=48 the C_T read is 4.3e-4 (-86%) after 20 steps and 7.8e-3 (+148%) after 300 steps against the anchor 3.14e-3, i.e. no stationary C_T exists, so no tier is admissible for the 3% judgement; the archived three-tier ladders are pre-asymptotic (observed p = -1.09 / -1.59), so the Roache GCI is undefined as well. Failure mode = resolution-dominated (the two closures agree to 0.2% at the anchor Re), not tau- or collision-model-dominated.
verdict.what_would_be_needed: a wall-modelled lattice at L ~ 450 cells per hull (y+ ~ 500, ~2.4e9 cells, ~170 GiB of distributions) - 4.7x the finest tier per dimension and far beyond the available hardware; wall-resolved would need L ~ 2e5.
